# 🎬 Media Bar Arrives on Jellyfin 12

Media Bar **3.0.0.0** brings support for **Jellyfin 12**, including compatibility with both the classic desktop experience and Jellyfin's newer modern web layout.

> ## 🙌 Huge thanks to MakD and the upstream contributors
>
> Media Bar itself is the work of **MakD and the contributors to the upstream Media Bar project**. The plugin I maintain is primarily a Jellyfin wrapper around that work, exposing configuration and integration points so it can be installed and managed cleanly as a Jellyfin plugin.
>
> A huge amount of effort has gone into keeping Media Bar working across Jellyfin's changing web interface, especially for Jellyfin 12. The features, UI work and frontend improvements in this release are built on that upstream work, and the credit for that belongs to **MakD and everyone contributing there**.
>
> My part is largely packaging, integrating and exposing that work through Jellyfin's plugin system.

## ✨ New Features

* Added support for **Jellyfin 12**.
* Added support for Jellyfin 12's **modern React/MUI home screen layout**, alongside the existing classic desktop layout.
* Updated the bundled Media Bar frontend to the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream version.
* Added Jellyfin 12-specific styling so Media Bar integrates correctly with the new web-client shell while retaining the existing appearance on the classic layout.
* Media Bar continues to ship its frontend assets directly with the plugin, ensuring the version displayed in Jellyfin matches the plugin version you've installed.

## 🛠️ Improvements

* Synced Media Bar with the latest Jellyfin 12-compatible upstream work.
* Improved Media Bar placement within the Jellyfin 12 home screen across both supported layouts.
* Improved layout behaviour on taller displays, ensuring Jellyfin's home-screen rows remain below the Media Bar content rather than overlapping its controls.
* Improved localisation handling when loading Jellyfin's translation chunks.
* Retained support for the **Get updates early** option for users who explicitly want to track unreleased upstream Media Bar changes.

## 🪲 Bug Fixes

* Fixed Media Bar being inserted in the wrong position when using Jellyfin 12's modern layout (#181).
* Fixed translated Media Bar strings falling back to English or producing JSON decoding errors for some languages (#185).
* Fixed home-screen rows overlapping Media Bar buttons on taller viewports.
* Fixed Jellyfin 12 layout differences that could cause Media Bar to render incorrectly compared with Jellyfin 10.11.

## ⚠️ Compatibility

* **Media Bar 3.0.0.0 supports Jellyfin 10.11.11 and Jellyfin 12.**
* Users on older Jellyfin 10.x versions should remain on a compatible **2.x** Media Bar release.
* Jellyfin 12 support includes both the **classic Desktop layout** and the newer **modern React/MUI layout**.
* A compatible **File Transformation 3.x** release is required.
* If you're using the **Get updates early** option, unreleased upstream Media Bar changes may behave differently from the frontend bundled and tested with this plugin release.

## Contributors

* austinnorgaard
* judarange

## ❤️ Support

If you enjoy using my Jellyfin plugins and want to support the time that goes into building, maintaining, and improving them, you can do so on [Ko-fi](https://ko-fi.com/IAmParadox27).

Thank you for using the plugins and being part of the community.

versions.changelog:
Requests og Kalender i burger-menuen.

Når Jellyfin 12 kører med den gamle skuffe - f.eks. med New Badges' burger-knap
på brede skærme - lægges de to links nu også ind der, lige under Hjem. Menuen
lukker af sig selv, når man klikker på dem.

Styres af de indstillinger, der allerede findes (Requests-fanen og
Kalender-fanen). Ingen nye indstillinger.

Kun Jellyfin 12.

- Menupillen øverst findes nu også i et halvt vindue: ikoner, med navnet på den side du er på, og et hint på resten. På en telefon ligger alt i menuen som før.
- Den valgte knap i pillen er hvid i stedet for blå.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Hele topbaren i én knapgruppe på Jellyfin 12.

- Film, Serier og dine andre biblioteker er nu med i knapgruppen, efter Favoritter og før Tilføj og Kalender. Før stod de uden for, så gruppen så ud som en bar, der stoppede halvvejs.
- Det bibliotek, du er inde i, er fyldt ud i gruppen.
- Ingen tynd kant rundt om gruppen længere - over banneret lignede den en rest af den gamle topbar. Gruppen har nu en mørk, let sløret baggrund i stedet.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Ny topbar på Jellyfin 12.

- Hjem, Favoritter, Tilføj og Kalender er samlet i én knapgruppe, hvor den side, du er på, er fyldt ud. Før var Hjem slet ikke med, og den aktive side blev kun vist med blå tekst.
- Kortere navne: "Tilføj" og "Kalender" (på engelsk "Request" og "Calendar"), så topbaren også er plads til på en bærbar.
- Tilføj og Kalender virker nu også fra andre sider end forsiden - før skete der ingenting.
- Rettet: efter at have åbnet Kalender kunne både Tilføj og Kalender stå markeret, og i sidemenuen på mobilen kunne tre punkter være markeret på én gang.
- Rettet: at skifte fra Tilføj eller Kalender til Hjem eller Favoritter kunne vise to faner oven i hinanden.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Forsiden indlæses hurtigere.

- Kalenderens hukommelse - alle de titler, den har set - ligger nu i sin egen fil på serveren i stedet for i plugin-indstillingerne. Indstillingerne hentes af alle browsere ved hver sideindlæsning og var vokset til over 100 KB; nu er de få KB. Flytningen sker af sig selv, når serveren starter.
- Scriptet caches af browseren og hentes kun igen, når plugin'et er opdateret.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.2.2.0.

Udgivelseskalenderen viser ikke længere gamle film som Point Break og The Godfather.

TMDB registrerer hver gang en film bliver vist på tv eller lagt på en streamingtjeneste - i alle lande. Kalenderen tog den første dato den fandt, så en fransk tv-visning af Point Break fra 1991 dukkede op som en kommende udgivelse. Nu gælder:

- Film der allerede ligger i biblioteket, vises ikke i kalenderen.
- Kalenderen bruger den tidligste streamingdato, ikke den første der står på listen.
- En dato mere end to år efter filmens premiere er en genudgivelse og vises ikke.

Til Jellyfin 12.

"Test forbindelse"-knappen ser nu rigtig ud ved siden af Gem.

Efter sidste udgave var Gem-knappen tegnet om til Jellyfin 12's stil, men "Test forbindelse" lige under den sad tilbage i den gamle grå udgave, så de to knapper så ud til at være lige vigtige.

Den er nu en omridset knap i temaets farve — samme størrelse som Gem, men tydeligt den sekundære af de to, præcis som Jellyfin 12 selv tegner et sådant knappepar.

Kun udseende. Knappen gør nøjagtig det samme som før.

Indstillingssiden er tegnet om, så den ser ud som resten af Jellyfin 12.

Jellyfin 12 har lavet sine egne indstillingssider om: felterne er nu fyldte bokse med en lille etiket øverst i selve feltet, i stedet for en label ovenover. Denne side fulgte stadig den gamle stil og stak derfor ud fra alt andet i dashboardet.

Felter, afkrydsningsfelter, overskrifter og Gem-knappen matcher nu Jellyfin 12's egne — samme højde, samme afrunding, samme farver. Farverne hentes fra Jellyfin 12's eget tema, så siden også følger med hvis du skifter tema.

Kun udseende. Der er ikke ændret noget i hvad siden gør, eller i indstillingerne selv. På Jellyfin 10.11 ser siden ud præcis som før — den nye stil slås kun til, hvis serveren rent faktisk er 12.

Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12.

Fanerne "Tilføj Film/Serie" og "Udgivelseskalender" er flyttet med. Jellyfin 12 har lavet hele den øverste menulinje om, og den gamle fanerække findes stadig i siden men bliver aldrig tegnet — så fanerne blev lagt et sted ingen kunne se dem. De sidder nu i den rigtige menulinje sammen med Favoritter, Film og Serier, og i menuen i siden på telefon.

Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende adgangsnøglen på (X-Emby-Token), så alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt. Uden det svarede serveren 401.

Indstillingssiden kunne ikke åbnes på Jellyfin 12. Pluginet kørte, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun siden, hvis den selv beder om at komme i menuen.

Accentfarven læses nu direkte fra temaet. Før blev den gættet ved at male en usynlig knap med Jellyfins egne klasser og aflæse farven — men Jellyfin 12 tegner sine knapper på en ny måde hvor den klasse ikke findes, så gættet slog fejl og faldt tilbage til en fast farve.

Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan kun installeres der. Kører du stadig 10.11, bliver du på den forrige udgave, som virker uændret — serveren vælger selv den rigtige. Grunden til at der skal være to: 10.11 og 12 kører på hver sin udgave af .NET, så det samme build kan ikke køre begge steder.

versions.changelog:
Understøtter nu Jellyfin 12.

Adgangsnøglen: Jellyfin 12 afviser den gamle måde at sende den på (X-Emby-Token). Det ramte Subtitle Guard hårdere end de andre plugins — tolv forskellige kald sendte den gamle vej, og de svarede alle 401 på Jellyfin 12. I praksis betød det at alt det der foregår fra selve siden holdt op med at virke: workers, køen, historikken, knapperne på detaljesiden. Alle kald bruger nu det almindelige Authorization-felt.

Indstillingssiden kunne slet ikke åbnes på Jellyfin 12. Pluginet kørte, men dets side under Dashboard → Plugins var der ikke, og der stod ingen fejl nogen steder. Det er den side hvor workers tilmeldes, så uden den kunne en ny worker ikke sættes op. Jellyfin 12's nye dashboard viser kun siden, hvis den selv beder om at komme i menuen.

Denne udgave er bygget til Jellyfin 12 og kan kun installeres der. Kører du stadig 10.11, bliver du på 2.1.0.0, som virker uændret — serveren vælger selv den rigtige. Grunden til at der skal være to: 10.11 og 12 kører på hver sin udgave af .NET, så det samme build kan ikke køre begge steder.

versions.changelog:
**Drop-down menus in the theme's look, and a title over the poster that
makes way for the hover buttons.** Jellyfin's drop-down fields - the item
page's audio and subtitle menus, "Add to playlist", the settings - showed
the browser's own grey list; in Chrome and Edge they now take the Dialogs &
menus look and open downwards. With the title printed over the poster, the
watched / favorite / menu buttons were hidden under it and greyed by its
gradient; the title now fades (or slides) away while the pointer is on the
card. All of it is plain CSS, so "CSS only" has it too.

Updating is enough - the plugin brings the CSS in Branding up to date at
startup, and open pages pick it up on their own (a browser holding the old
page in its cache may need one Ctrl+F5).

Drop-down menus

- Dialogs & menus: Jellyfin's drop-down fields take the menus' look - style, color, opacity, blur, corners - with the chosen entry marked in the accent: the item page's version / video / audio / subtitle menus, "Add to playlist" (the one music users meet) and "Add to collection", the user settings for the home screen, playback and subtitles, the metadata editor. They are native selects, and on a computer or a phone the browser drew their list itself, in its own grey, out of any theme's reach. Chrome and Edge (135 and up) now draw it as part of the page (`appearance: base-select`); other browsers keep their own list, in the theme's colors. The TV opens Jellyfin's own menu, which was themed already. Plain CSS, so "CSS only" has it too.
- The lists open downwards. The browser picks the side with more room, so a field in the lower row of the item page opened upwards; below comes first now, a list that does not fit there gets shorter (it scrolls), and only a field at the very bottom of the window opens upwards.

Cards

- Cards: with the title over the image, the hover buttons (watched, favorite, menu) appeared under it - both sit in the bottom corner, and the title lay on top and took their clicks. The title now makes way while the pointer is on the card: it fades out (the default) or slides down as it fades, and comes back when the pointer leaves. The choice is under the title setting (*Cards → The title when the pointer is on the card*, shown for "Over the image" while the hover buttons are on); "Stays" keeps it as before. Only where the buttons appear - not on the TV or a phone, not on series, seasons and collections whose buttons are hidden, and not on the Seerr rows' cards (their button sits in the middle). Plain CSS, so it works with "CSS only" too.
- Fixed: with the title over the image the hover buttons and the bottom card badges were grey and dull - the dark gradient under the title was painted over them (the same layer, and last in the card). It lies under them now, and while the title makes way the gradient goes with it; Jellyfin's own veil over a hovered card stays.

**A theme applied shows at once, the music player follows the theme, and
"CSS only" is CSS only everywhere.** Jellyfin's client held the branding
CSS for a minute, so open pages kept the old theme after an Apply; the
client script now swaps in the fresh one - on the next navigation within a
second, on a page left open within ten. The music player takes the Player
section's look - until now its bar and sliders stayed in Jellyfin's grey
and blue whatever the theme said. Applied, "CSS only" takes the admin look
off the plugin page at once, the CSS it writes holds nothing for the admin
pages, and a theme exported in that mode is a CSS theme, so an import gives
the same look. Plus a fix for the Sidebar layout, which broke the admin
pages when they followed the defaults.

Updating is enough - the plugin brings the CSS in Branding up to date at
startup, and the client script's address carries the version, so a fresh
page load picks the new one up (a browser holding the old page in its cache
may need one Ctrl+F5).

A theme applied reaches open pages at once

- Fixed: a theme just applied took a minute or more to show on the user-facing pages - on the admin pages it was there at once. Jellyfin's client keeps the branding CSS it fetched for a minute before it asks again (and a tab left open did not ask until something nudged it). The theme block now carries a stamp, a new `/Jellycanvas/CssStamp` tells the current one in a few bytes, and the client script asks for it when a page loads, on every navigation, when the window or the tab comes back, and every ten seconds while the page is in view; it also watches the client's copy, which the client renders again after a navigation. An older copy is switched off and the fresh CSS goes in over it until the client catches up - a navigation shows the new theme within a second, a page just left open within ten. With "CSS only" there is no script, and Jellyfin's minute stays.
- The client script runs for an applied theme even without a feature of its own (that check is its job then).
- The startup refresh compares the stamp: the date line in the block made it rewrite Branding on every start, even with nothing changed.

The music player

- The music player follows the Player section: its bar along the bottom takes the control bar's style (solid, glass, gradient and the rest, its color, opacity, blur), floats and rounds like it, and its buttons take the buttons' size. The position and volume sliders - in the bar and on the queue page - take the progress slider's color and the position ones its height. Until now all of it stayed in Jellyfin's stock grey and hard-coded blue.
- Sliders anywhere else (a settings page, say) take the accent instead of Jellyfin blue.
- Fixed: with the Sidebar layout the music bar ran under the sidebar and covered its bottom (the user button among it); it starts where the content does now.
- Test server: `test\Make-Music.ps1` adds a music library - three made-up albums of generated tones, tagged and with covers - to check the music pages against a theme.

CSS only

- Fixed: after "CSS only" was applied, the plugin page itself - an admin page - kept the custom Dashboard look until it was reloaded. The client script running in it went on with what it had fetched when the page loaded. The designer now swaps it for what the server serves after every Apply and every Remove: nothing after CSS only (the admin pages turn stock at once), and the fresh admin look after an ordinary Apply, which until now also waited for a reload.
- CSS only: the theme no longer writes its rules for the admin pages - without the script they never reach them (Jellyfin renders Branding on the user-facing pages only), so they were dead weight.
- Share: a theme exported in "CSS only" mode carries the CSS look only. The script's features were hidden from its author, yet the export took whatever they still held (from before the switch, or from an import) - so an import brought a slideshow, badges or an admin look nobody had seen with that theme. The admin pages are left out now (their panel settings, "Theme the Dashboard" and the Dashboard tab's document), and of the script's features only their switches go along, turned off (the slideshow, the badges, the item page's banner, the info bar's close button) - an import gives the same CSS version, and the theme site no longer lists such a theme as needing File Transformation or styling the admin pages. The importer's own "CSS only" choice, buttons and Seerr stay theirs, as before. The Share section says so while CSS only is on.
- Designer: unticking "CSS only" brings the script features back into the preview straight away; until now they came back only with the next change to a script setting.

The admin pages

- Fixed: with the Sidebar layout and the theme on the Dashboard, the admin pages fell apart - their top bar was turned into the sidebar column and went off the screen, and the content slid under the admin menu. The admin pages have a menu of their own on the left, so the sidebar now stays on the user-facing pages and the admin bar docks next to the menu as before. The Dashboard tab no longer offers a layout either; it shows the bar's own settings.

The designer

- Designer: rows show where they do something - the "Play" label only while the other buttons have no labels (with labels on, Play has one anyway), the logo's height for the Jellyfin icon or a custom image and its width for a custom image only, and the info bar's settings only while the bar is on.

**The loading ring gets a look of its own, and a season's episodes get
their badges.** The ring Jellyfin shows while a stream starts can take one
of six styles, a color, size, speed, a glow and a disc behind it - and even
left alone it now follows the theme's accent instead of Jellyfin blue. The
episodes on a season's page carry the card badges, the home slideshow's
button picks its icon from a list, and the Dashboard's device cards lose
the dark boxes a lighter now-playing veil left behind their text.

Updating is enough - the plugin brings the CSS in Branding up to date at
startup, and the client script's address carries the version, so a fresh
page load picks the new one up (a browser holding the old page in its cache
may need one Ctrl+F5).

The player

- Player: the loading ring - the one Jellyfin shows while a stream starts (and, being the same element, while a page loads) - has settings of its own (Player -> Loading ring): Jellyfin's ring, a ring, a double ring, an orbiting dot, a pulse or three dots; its color (empty = the accent), size, line thickness and speed; a glow in its color; and a dark or frosted disc behind it. The player preview shows it in the middle, and Ctrl+click on it opens these settings. Jellyfin paints its ring blue by hard-coded value, so even untouched it now takes the theme's accent.

Home slideshow

- Home slideshow: the button's icon is picked from a list - info, play, play in a circle, a screen with play, arrows, open, eye, film strip, cinema, compass, star, heart, three dots, or none - with the chosen icon shown next to the label. "Another one" brings back the name field for any Material icon, and a theme with an icon outside the list opens with that field.
- Fixed: the home slideshow's button style did nothing in the designer's preview - the button kept the look it had when the slideshow first appeared. The slideshow writes its own stylesheet, and when the script started again with new settings (the preview restarts it on every change) it found the old sheet and left it alone. A real client loads the page afresh, so the applied style was right there. The sheet is rewritten now, and it goes with the rest of the script's leftovers when the script stops.

The admin pages

- Fixed: on the Dashboard, a device card with nothing playing showed dark boxes behind its lines of text as soon as "Darkening over a playing session's picture" was changed. The darkening went on every stack inside the card - and an idle card is built of several, one per line - instead of the one that covers a playing card's picture; it now goes only there, and only on a card that has a picture.
- Dashboard: the text on a device card without a picture follows the card's color - the theme's text where it reads well on it (4.5 : 1), otherwise white or near-black, whichever stands out more. The card is the accent laid over the panel; a light accent no longer leaves white text on yellow.

Card badges

- Card badges on a season's episodes: the season's page lists them as rows, not cards, and they had none. A list row now gets badges on its picture like a card (a library shown as a list too); a small thumbnail - a queue, a playlist - stays bare.

**Older TVs get the whole theme, the item page gets a real banner, and the
theme can run as plain CSS.** On a TV before Chromium 105 (most LG webOS sets
in use) nine rules in ten were dropped as soon as the Dashboard tab had a
setting of its own; the admin pages' scope no longer needs `:has()`, and the
poster tint that still used it goes by Jellyfin's own mark. The item page's
banner is a strip at the top of the page, the way Jellyfin draws its own,
with a fade and a background of its own for the page below. "CSS only"
leaves the client script out entirely for those who want nothing injected
into the web client. Plus a security pass: the anonymous random background
respects every account's access, and text in the CSS and the script is
escaped more strictly.

Updating is enough - the plugin brings the CSS in Branding up to date at
startup, the client script reloads by itself, and a theme saved with a
setting that moved is read the new way.

The item page banner

- Item page banner: "Banner" is a strip now, not the page - the item's banner, or else its thumb (or its backdrop), fills the top of the page from behind the top bar down to the bottom of the title bar and scrolls with the page, the way Jellyfin's own details banner sits; the page below keeps its background and a rotating backdrop pauses there. Only "Backdrop" covers the whole page. The separate "Thumb" choice is gone (the thumb is the banner's own fallback); a saved theme with it gets the strip.
- Item page banner: a chosen banner that the item does not have falls back to its thumb first, then to the backdrop - films rarely have a banner but most have a thumb ("Náhled" in a Czech Jellyfin, which is what "Edit images" shows). The options and the hint use Jellyfin's own names, and the dimming label no longer claims the background's dimming applies.
- Item page banner: a background of its own for the page under the strip - the page's own (the background settings, as before), one colour, or a gradient (from / to / direction). It applies while an item page shows the strip; every other page keeps its background.
- Item page banner: a fade at the bottom of the strip - how far up it reaches (0 = a hard edge, as before) and the colour it fades into (empty = the page background). Shown for the banner strip only; the full-page backdrop has its own dimming.
- Background: "On an item's page show that item's own backdrop" is gone - it did the same as the item page's "The item's picture behind its page" with Backdrop, which stays (with its own dimming and "keep the top in view", and over any background). A theme saved with the old switch gets that banner, dimmed as the background was; the designer moves it over when a theme is loaded or imported, device views included.
- Item page banner, fixed in four places. The designer's preview never picked a banner change up (the banner lives in the client script, and only a background change refreshed the script there), so the section seemed to do nothing. A random backdrop that was still loading when an item's page opened landed on top of the item's picture a moment later - the rotation looked as if it never stopped; only the picture asked for last is shown now, and a random one fetched before the page opened stays out. The banner's own dimming and "top of the picture" were ignored whenever the background already had a layer of its own (a random backdrop, say); they apply to the item's picture now, and the random pictures elsewhere keep the background's settings. And an episode or a season without a banner or a thumb borrows its series' before falling back to the backdrop - the designer says so, as films from TMDB rarely have a banner at all.
- Fixed: the item page's banner with Backdrop showed nothing over a background of the theme's own that does not rotate (a custom picture, a colour, a gradient, a random picture without rotation). The layer the item's picture lies on was set up only by the rotation or by the switch above.

Older TVs

- Fixed: on older TVs the whole theme was gone as soon as the Dashboard tab had a setting of its own. The admin pages' scope was written as `html:has(body.dashboardDocument)`, so every default rule carried `:not(:has(...))` - and a browser before Chromium 105 (webOS before 23, which is most LG TVs in use; older Tizen) drops a rule it cannot read, which was about nine rules in ten. The scope is a class now (`html.jc-dashboard`) that the client script sets on admin pages - the same script that carries the theme there.
- Fixed: "Translucent tint over the poster" (Watched & progress) was a thin line on older TVs. The rule that stretches the footer holding the progress bar used `:has()`, which a browser before Chromium 105 cannot read; it goes by Jellyfin's own mark for that footer now.
- Older TVs (Chromium 53 and up): the content under a taller TV bar keeps its offset (the `max()` it used needs Chromium 79, so a plain value comes first), and the islands of the TV bar keep their spacing where a flex gap is not known.

CSS only

- "CSS only" (Companion plugins): the theme runs without the client script - nothing is put into index.html, so File Transformation is not used - and the designer offers only what plain CSS can do: the sections and rows that need the script go, and so does the Dashboard tab (the admin pages are reached through the script alone). TV and Mobile keep working: they are CSS scoped to the layout Jellyfin itself marks. A shared theme does not carry the choice, and an imported one does not change it.

The admin pages

- Dashboard tab: "Jellyfin's own Dashboard" keeps the theme off the admin pages altogether, whatever the tab says; the tab's settings grey out meanwhile and the preview shows the stock admin pages.
- Dashboard: the veil Jellyfin lays over a playing session's picture (70 % black) can be set (Admin pages -> "Darkening over a playing session's picture"); below Jellyfin's the text gets a shadow to stay readable.
- Fixed: with the theme on the Dashboard, a device card showed an empty box where the picture of what is playing belongs. The rule that recolours the Jellyfin-blue placeholder behind device cards also cleared their background image - and Jellyfin keeps that placeholder class on a playing session's card, with the item's picture set over it. Only the colour changes now.

Security and speed

- Security: the random background picks only items every enabled account may see. Its address is anonymous (the login page uses it, and a CSS `url()` cannot carry a token), so it cannot tell who is looking - and until now it could put a backdrop from a library a child's account is kept out of, or one rated above that account's limit, on the login page or behind that child's home screen. Library access, the parental rating and blocked tags of every account are respected now.
- Security: text the theme writes into a CSS string (the `content:` of a label) loses every control character, not just line breaks - a form feed also ends a CSS string and would let the rest of the text be read as rules.
- Security: the settings baked into the client script escape `<`, `>`, `&` and `'` (before, only `</` was defused), so the script stays whole even when pasted inline into an HTML page by an injector plugin. Letters of every language stay readable.
- Faster: "Slow panning animation" moves the picture's layer instead of the picture inside it. It animated `background-position`, which makes the browser restyle and repaint a full-screen picture every frame; a `transform` runs on the compositor. A home page at rest with a panning random background went from about 120 ms of main-thread work per 8 seconds to 16 ms (Chrome, desktop) - on a weak TV it was most of what the page cost. It looks the same, portrait phones included.
- Seerr posters: the disk cache no longer grows for ever - posters nobody asked for in 30 days go (checked at most once a day). A poster is written aside and moved in whole, so two requests at once never read a half-written file; after a server restart a poster already on disk is served straight away instead of a 404 until Seerr has answered again; a download is capped at 4 MB.

The designer

- The designer's device views show only what that scope can use: a setting that belongs to one device (the phone's card radius, the TV's focus ring) stays out of the other's view, "hide this on the TV / on phones" is offered in Defaults alone - inside a device's own view the setting already is that device's - and the hover rows (hover effect, hover buttons on a poster, lift on hover, a hover color) are gone from the TV and the phone, which have no pointer. The rows are marked by their setting path, so one added later lands in the right view by itself.
- Buttons: "Mark the selected button" (on by default) - under glass, glow and the other looks the stock "selected" fill was painted over, so a row of tabs (the designer's own Default / TV / Mobile / Dashboard among them) no longer said which one was open. The selected one gets the accented look and an outline. The designer's own tabs are marked that way whatever the setting.
- Ctrl+click in the preview: the watched tick and the progress bar open "Watched & progress" instead of the card's look (like the badges, they let clicks through to the poster, so they are found by their place), and the login page's heading and buttons open the Login section rather than the font - their text is a setting there. A second click on the same row keeps its highlight for the full time.
- The bar's corner radius is offered where it does something: with an islands bar the corners come from the island radius, so the row is hidden there.
- Designer: a row hidden for want of the client script stayed on screen when it was a checkbox (Jellyfin's rows are display: flex, which beats the browser's own [hidden] rule) - the item page's banner switch among them.
- The Dashboard's plugin list shows a release as three numbers (1.2.4, not 1.2.4.0). Jellyfin lists the version the DLL carries, and a .NET assembly version always has four parts; the plugin now reports three unless the fourth is set - which only a test build does.

Other fixes

- Fixed: on an item's page a background of the theme's own was faded to the background's dimming - a random or custom picture, and the item's own backdrop the banner brings, all came out much darker than on the other pages. Jellyfin marks the background on an item's page (`withBackdrop`), and the theme faded that mark to dim Jellyfin's own backdrop; it does so only when Jellyfin's own backdrop is what shows.
- Fixed: the image search (Edit images -> search) could not be scrolled. The theme clips rounded dialogs with `overflow: hidden`, but some of Jellyfin's dialogs scroll on the dialog itself (`.scrollY` / `.smoothScrollY`) - those clip sideways only now and scroll as before. The admin pages' panel corners no longer reach MUI dialogs either, for the same reason.
- Fixed: a font chosen for the TV, the phone or the admin pages alone was never fetched - the Google Fonts import was built from the defaults only, so that scope asked for a font the page had not loaded and fell back to another. Every scope's font is imported now, at the top of the stylesheet where imports are allowed.
- Fixed: inside one device's scope the theme also wrote the other device's rules, which could never match (a phone's rule under `html.layout-tv`), and the TV / phone palette variables were written unscoped - so a value set for the admin pages reached every TV. Each scope now carries its own device's rules only, and names its layout once instead of twice.
- Card badges: the Slovak flag was a bare white-blue-red tricolour - at badge size, Russia's. It carries its coat of arms now, and so do the two others that had the same problem: Slovenia's (also Russia's without it) and Croatia's (the Netherlands' without the chequy shield).
- Code clean-up: comments that had drifted off the code they described, a leftover of the old full-page "Thumb" banner in the client script, and a portrait-phone override the new panning makes unnecessary.

**The admin pages get the theme, and a designer tab of their own.** Jellyfin 12
renders the branding CSS on the user-facing pages only, so the Dashboard came
up in the stock greys and blues however the palette was set - the designer's
preview showed it themed, the real thing was not. The theme reaches the admin
pages now, and they are a scope of their own next to TV and Mobile: an admin
can give the Dashboard a look that has nothing to do with what the users see.

Updating is enough - the plugin brings the CSS in Branding up to date at
startup, and the client script reloads by itself.

The admin pages

- The Dashboard carries the theme (the switch is on the Dashboard tab; it needs the client script).
- A tab of its own next to TV and Mobile: the admin pages can be set apart from the rest, and what is left alone follows the defaults. Ctrl+click on the Dashboard preview lands there, the tab shows only what the admin pages can use (no posters, player, item page or login form), and it drops rows that belong to the client (an item page's buttons, the library row, the rotating backdrop).
- A section of its own for the panels the admin pages are built from: opacity, color, corners, border, shadow, glass blur, and hiding the help links under the settings headings. Buttons and inputs there (a plugin page has the same ones) follow the Buttons section of that tab.
- The admin pages come with a MUI theme of their own: tables, grid toolbars, chips, selected rows and the alerts above a form kept Jellyfin's stock colors whatever the palette said. They follow the theme now, lists and cards count as panels too (the activity feed, the device cards, the admin menu take the panel corners), and a panel's rounded corners are no longer squared off by the toolbar above its table.
- The preview has a second admin page - a settings form - and Ctrl+click there maps to what the admin pages are made of: a panel opens the panel settings, a form row the buttons and inputs, bare page the background color.
- "Theme the Dashboard" is the way back to the defaults: ticking it puts the admin pages on the theme as it is set in Defaults and drops what the tab has of its own; the first change made there unticks it again, the Dashboard keeps that change, and the theme still reaches the admin pages.
- Fixed: the top bar ignored its own settings - the island layout has nothing to make there and the panel rules were painting over it. The admin bar is a plain bar now (color, radius, shadow apply) and a floating bar stays docked next to the menu.
- Fixed: the left menu could not be scrolled (the rounded drawer edge was clipping it).
- Fixed: a background set on the Dashboard tab did nothing - the admin pages' own normalisation painted the same element through a more specific rule, so a solid color or a gradient never showed.
- Fixed: and where it did show, the defaults' rotating backdrop painted over it a moment later - the client script knew the TV and the phone as scopes of their own, but an admin page counted as an ordinary desktop page. The admin pages follow the Dashboard's own background now, rotation and panning included.

Buttons

- The whole family of looks the bars and the player's control bar have - glass, glow, gradient, neo-brutalism, glowmorphism, claymorphism, neumorphism - on every kind of button the client has, and the same looks on the item page's Play button, the play button on posters, the "skip intro" button and the slideshow button.
- A switch to leave the top bar out of it (*Buttons and inputs -> Leave the buttons in the top bar out of it*). A frame or a fill around every library link turns the bar into a row of boxes; the links and the row under them keep Jellyfin's plain look while Play all and everything else follow the style.
- Fixed: the rows of the user settings menu (Profile, Display, Home screen...) are buttons, but only their corners followed the Buttons section; they wear the chosen look now.
- The radius sliders that went to 999 now end at 40 px with one notch past it for a fully rounded button (everything above about 25 px looks the same, which made the slider unusable).

Item page

- A banner of the item's own picture behind its page (*Item page -> Banner*): backdrop, banner or thumb, with dimming and the top of the picture kept in view. It is the look Jellyfin gives users who turn its own "details banner" on - this one comes from the theme, so everyone sees it whatever the background is set to.

Lighter on weak clients

- Card badges are placed only for cards near the screen, and the cards are watched (IntersectionObserver) instead of the grid being walked and measured on a timer. On a library of several hundred cards that was hundreds of layout reads a second and a visibly stuttering page; nothing is measured while scrolling now, placement takes six cards at a time in the browser's idle moments, and the re-measure after a resize or a new font only looks at cards near the screen.
- A burst of page changes wakes the script at most every 120 ms instead of every frame.

And the rest

- An update takes effect on its own: the generated CSS lives in Branding and was only written when someone pressed Apply, so after updating the plugin the server kept serving the CSS the previous version had made - fixes in it waited for a visit to the designer. The plugin now rebuilds that block at startup when this version would generate something different (the theme has to be on and the block present; an unchanged theme is not rewritten).
- The TV view drops the rotation and the panning rows while "Still background on TV" is on in Defaults - they do nothing there - and says where they went instead.
- Share / import points at the theme site (jellycanvas.jellyscope.cz): browsing, previewing and downloading are open to everyone, uploading needs an account there.
- The JSON export leaves out the whole Seerr section (address, key and the rows) and empties the preferred audio and subtitle languages - a theme from abroad should not arrive filtering for someone else's languages. Nothing in the running theme changes; only what leaves the server.

A bug-fix release. Several fixes and the new flat backgrounds live in the generated CSS: open the designer and press Apply once after updating; the client script reloads by itself.

- Fixed: a TV or phone background of its own (per-device settings) changed only the CSS part - the client script kept rotating the defaults' random backdrops there, so on the TV nothing seemed to change. The script now carries each device's own backdrop settings and follows the layout; the backdrop layer rules are scoped to the device too.
- Background: two flat sources - one color, or a gradient between two colors like the login page's (from / to / angle). Jellyfin's own backdrop goes; an item page can still show its own backdrop over it (the "item page" switch), dimmed as set.
- Login page: one flat color as the background (over the gradient; an image URL wins over both).
- Designer: a device tag on a slider row (a value the TV or the phone overrides) sat over the number box; it sits after the label now.
- Fixed: "hide scrollbars" (Misc) left the page's own scrollbar - the rule reached everything under the root but not the root itself. Apply once after updating.
- Designer: Ctrl+click on a scrollbar (the page's or a panel's) opens Misc at "hide scrollbars".
- Designer: the reset arrow on an overridden checkbox row toggled the checkbox instead (the label lay over the arrow).
- Card badges no longer react to the play button: it lies above them (its own z-index), and an admin who puts it in a badge corner moves one of the two. Before, the hover button counted as a fixed one while the pointer was on the card, and the hover zoom counted as a new card width, so the badges jumped about on hover. Sizes come from the layout width now, not the zoomed one.
- Card badges: a portrait poster is measured against a smaller reference width than a landscape card, so its badges are not smaller than the same card's on the home page (a 195px poster: full size; a phone's 104px poster: about nine tenths - the fitting shrinks only what does not fit).
- Designer: the TV and phone views no longer show rows that only make sense in the defaults - "Still background on TV" and "no play button on phones" (in a device view the setting itself is that device's).
- Fixed: the TV still background stayed over a playing video (its rule outranked the one that clears backdrops during playback). Apply the theme once after updating.
- Card badges: the corners of a card now share one size and are fitted together - nothing lies over another corner, the title strip or a fixed button. Long texts go short first, then all corners shrink together, then a column lies down into rows of two flags, then a corner moves past its neighbour, then badges come off the end; afterwards the size grows back as far as it fits, so badges are never smaller than they must be. A bottom corner no longer sits over the flags of a top one.
- Card badges: commas between the codes of a language pill ("CS, EN" - a small "CSEN" read as one odd word).

- Seerr rows: a poster opened through a custom button is addressed the way that button addresses Seerr (its host and base path), so the session the user has in that overlay applies - before, the link used the server-side Seerr address (a container name or a LAN address): a different origin with no session, often not reachable from the browser at all. New setting "Seerr address for links in the browser" for the plain new-tab links; empty = the same as the server address.

The play button settings and the phone fixes live in the generated CSS: open the designer and press Apply once after updating. The client script reloads by itself (its address now changes with the settings).

- Card badges on small cards (a phone, a dense grid): the two top corners shrink a little to sit side by side before one is moved past the other, the badges shrink as a whole (their padding follows the font), the inset is smaller, and the shrinking is decisive (two rounds) so a hair of overlap no longer sends a corner under the other; long texts go short before anything shrinks or moves - a sound name loses its layout or its codec (TrueHD Atmos 7.1 -> Atmos 7.1, DTS-HD 7.1 -> DTS-HD) and a language pill folds to two entries plus a count (CS EN FR DE -> CS EN +2). Test media: Oppenheimer and the first Severance episode (a landscape card) carry TrueHD 5.1 next to four flags and four codes. A column at the top - under a played tick, or moved past the other corner - now ends above the title strip and above the play button touch clients keep on every poster (a column too long first shrinks to fit, down to about three fifths - the fixed inset is not scaled, so the shrink really fits; one still too long lies down into rows of two flags, so it still reads as a column; only then does it drop extra flags, then badges); a play button placed in a top corner pushes that corner's badges under it, and bottom badges stay above a bottom one.
- Card badges on phones matched the preview only sometimes: the language pills used the icon font, and before that font had loaded the pill was measured with the icon's name spelled out - three times as wide - so the corners were placed for a pill that never was. The pills' icons are inline SVG now, badges wait for the page fonts (a few seconds at most) and are placed again when a font arrives later. The inset that clears the rounded corner is kept on a box's outer sides only, which leaves narrow cards room for both corners at full size; a column under a played tick shrinks down to half before it lies down into rows (small flags under the tick beat a block of rows); a folded block is never narrower than its pill.
- The client script's address carries a stamp of the settings, so a phone or a PWA that cached the script picks the new one up after any save (before, it could keep running the old script until a hard refresh).
- Designer: the import box empties once its JSON has been taken over.
- Fixed: with "show the text next to the icons" on the item page, the button row ran off a phone's screen; phones now label the play button only and the row wraps if it still has to.
- Seerr rows: a poster's Seerr page can open through a custom toolbar button that points at Seerr (its overlay, or in place) instead of a second Seerr tab - "Open a poster's Seerr page" in the Seerr section; new tab stays the default.
- Cards: the play button on posters has its own settings (Cards section, "Play button on posters"): style (Jellyfin's own, accent, dark, white, glass), a color of its own, fill opacity, a hover color (empty = a little brighter with the icon in the accent color, as Jellyfin does), corner radius, position (Jellyfin's own, middle or a corner - a bottom corner starts above an overlaid title, and on the web above the small mark / favourite / menu group), size, and "no play button on phones". Applies to the web's hover button (which keeps its 1.4x hover zoom at any size) and the fixed one touch clients draw - both the new card's button group and the old home-page card's button; the TV has none, so the rows stay out of the TV view.
- Designer: Ctrl+click on a card badge in the preview opens the badges section (the badges let clicks through to the poster, so they are found by their place, like the info strip).

Several fixes live in the generated CSS: open the designer and press Apply once after updating.

- Per-device settings: the designer edits the defaults (web and everything else) or, with the switch at the top, the TV or the phone - the same sections, and a value changed there applies to that device only while everything else keeps following the defaults; changed rows are marked and reset with one click, and in the default view a row a device overrides carries that device's tag (click it to get there). Ctrl+click in a TV or phone preview opens the device's own value when it has one, otherwise the default. The CSS carries a scoped copy of the theme for each device with changes, and the defaults stay off such a device (a full bar on the TV no longer shows the web's islands through it). In the TV and phone views the sidebar layout (a desktop thing), the other device's sections and the info bar and logo (defaults with their own "hide on TV / phone" switches) are out of the way; the TV and phone sections live in their device's view only.
- The preview reminds you of Ctrl+click: a hint follows the mouse until the first click, and with Ctrl held the element under the mouse is framed and the hint names the section a click opens (gone as soon as Ctrl is released). The info strip - a pseudo-element with nothing to click on - is found by its place, so Ctrl+click on it opens the info bar section. The slideshow (its logo, overview and button land on their own switches) and the Seerr rows open their own sections instead of the toolbar buttons.
- On load the designer no longer opens the presets and colors once the theme has been applied, nor the companion plugins while one is installed and working.
- Fixed: the mobile card radius did nothing (it set only the theme variable).
- Fixed: with "hide the hover buttons on series, seasons and collections" on, a series in a Seerr row lost its open button too (the card carries the type); the rows' cards are exempt from it, and from "hide the hover buttons" altogether - their one button is the way to the title. Apply the theme once after updating - the rule lives in the generated CSS.
- Fixed: on TV the split bar read as one long island with only the icons apart - Jellyfin lets the left group grow across the row; it now ends at its content. The default logo also sits in a square box (Jellyfin 12 draws its icon in the old banner's 13.2em box, leaving a gap before a custom button).
- Fixed: the home slideshow crept down the page while scrolling (the gap it keeps under the top bar was re-measured against the viewport on every sync, so each scroll pushed it - and everything under it - further down).

- TV: a still background - no rotation and no panning on TV, one random backdrop; an item page still shows its own backdrop.
- Card badges follow the card width (down to about three quarters on a dense library grid), two corners of one edge that would run into each other stack instead, a pill never runs past the card, and the bottom corners sit right above an overlaid title (they were lifted twice).

Designer

Theme

- Bar: full-width top bar, top bar split into islands, or a vertical

- Cards: rounding, hover effects, shadow, border, text placement,

Script features (with File Transformation or a JS injector)

versions.changelog: If the plugin stopped working with "The poster overlay state file ... could not be read", this release is for you. The state file is now written atomically, so a server that dies mid-write can no longer leave it empty - which is what happened on the reference server when the VM was killed during the nightly run. An image uploaded just before a crash is now recognised on the next run, and a cached original without a record is never overwritten. New task "Rebuild poster overlay state": run it with the dry run on first. It rebuilds a record only where drawing today's badges onto the cached original gives the cover on the item again, and lists everything else by name without touching it. Do not delete a damaged state file - the old error message advised that, and it was wrong.

Nothing changes visibly in this one. The preview picker on the settings page now tells the server explicitly not to substitute collections for the films inside them when searching. That was already the behaviour, but only because Jellyfin happens to switch it off for searches by itself - and because the search box never queries with fewer than two characters. Neither is something this plugin controls, so it now says what it means. Badges, rendering and the scheduled task are untouched.

The report about folder names that disagree with the video stream over HDR is now a setting, and it is off by default. It only says something if your folder names carry release tags - if you name folders "Film (Year)", every HDR title would be counted as a disagreement. Turn it on under Operation if the tags are there. The badges follow the video stream either way, with the report on or off.

Names the file behind "the image could not be decoded" instead of only the film, so a broken cover can be found without searching by hand - and fixes a case where that message could not be reached at all, because the renderer threw on a file its decoder cannot open rather than reporting it. The HDR/DV disagreement between folder name and video stream is now summarised once per run instead of printed for every film: it is the ordinary case, not an exception, and it was burying the messages worth reading. The v12 build now targets Jellyfin 12.0.0 rather than a release candidate.

Fixes a badge that could not be taken off again. When an item lost its last badge - a duplicate was deleted, or it never really had a twin - the plugin was supposed to put the untouched cover back, and never did: the restore asked for a lock its own caller was already holding, then failed silently. A run with 222 items to restore restored none of them and reported a missing cache that was present. If your library carries labels that no longer apply, the next nightly run clears them.

Fixes the audio badge appearing on films that have no second copy at all.

Peers were matched by any shared provider id, which swept in TmdbCollection - an id every film of a series carries. All fifteen Star Wars films therefore counted as copies of one another, their audio formats differed, and a badge appeared where the rule says there should be none. Only ids that name a title are used now: IMDb, TMDb, TVDB and the custom id an NFO can set.

Also fixes the badge never appearing in the previous version, where copies were grouped by Jellyfin's presentation key. That key groups the rows of a series, but for a film it falls back to the item's own id unless the files were merged as alternate versions by hand, so two ordinary copies never shared it.

The badge itself is unchanged: ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on, drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it, describing the track in the language you set rather than the technically best one.

It was grouping copies of a film by Jellyfin's presentation key, which groups the rows of a series but not of a film: for a film that key falls back to the item's own id unless the files were merged as alternate versions by hand, so two ordinary copies never shared it and the badge was skipped every time. Copies are now matched by provider id.

Adds an audio-format badge - ATMOS, DTS-X, TRUEHD, DTS-HD and so on - drawn only where two copies of the same title actually differ in it. Off by default.

The restriction is the point. Measured on a library of 2,346 films: of 105 groups holding more than one copy of a film, 7 differ in nothing the existing badges could show except the audio format. Every other film has no second copy at all, so a format badge there describes a file nobody is comparing to anything.

Which track it describes is configurable, as a list of languages, best first - the first one any track carries wins. This matters more than it sounds: 437 films carry several languages in different formats, typically a German AC3 beside an English DTS, and taking the best track badges such a film "DTS", which is true about the file and about a track its owner never selects. Setting a language therefore draws fewer badges rather than more, which is the intent.

Spelling is forgiving because the server is asked rather than a table in the plugin: "de", "ger", "deu" and "German" all name one language, for every language Jellyfin knows. A file with a single track always reports that one, whatever the preference says.

The pinned preview - the copy of the picture at the right edge of the window - could be closed and then not reopened. There is a labelled button beside the style buttons now, and whether you want the panel is remembered between visits.

Also finishes a correction from the previous version. Twelve style rules were applying to the whole Jellyfin interface rather than to the plugin's own settings page, four of them since long before the preview existed. Nothing collided in practice, which is why it would have gone on unnoticed. There are no exceptions: an earlier attempt claimed the pinned panel sits outside the page and could not be scoped, which was reasoned rather than checked - it is a child of the page, and being fixed-position does not change that.

Fixes the preview opening at the poster's stored size and covering the settings page. Only the previous version is affected - the preview arrived there.

A percentage limit on the image was no limit at all in that spot: it resolves against its container, and the floating panel is fixed-position with no width of its own, so the container simply grew with the picture. The panel now has a width, and the image is bounded in both directions, since a poster arrives at 1000x1500 and upwards.

Also corrects eight style rules that were applying to the whole Jellyfin interface rather than to the plugin's own settings page. Nothing collided in practice, which is why it would otherwise have gone unnoticed. Two rules genuinely have to reach outside the page and now say so; the rest are scoped, and both facts are held in place by tests.

The settings page now previews on a real item, drawn by the server through exactly the code a run uses. It used to imitate the badges in SVG on a mock poster - a second implementation of the drawing rules, which had already drifted from the real one: the centred positions had to be taught to both, and the imitation estimated text width where the renderer measures it, so no pill was ever quite the right width.

The page sends the settings as they stand, saved or not, so a change can be looked at before it is kept. Nothing is written while previewing - not the item, not the cached original, not the stored configuration.

Two things come with using a real item. There is a search box to choose which one, and on opening the page offers one that already carries badges, because picking at random would usually show an untouched poster and look like a fault. And when no badge is drawn the page now says why - the category is off, the item is on the exception list, or the episode has no second copy and the category only badges where that tells two apart. An unbadged preview and a broken one used to look identical.

The settings sections fold away and remember how they were left.

For anyone driving the plugin from a script: POST PosterOverlays/Preview/{itemId} takes a configuration and returns the image it would produce, changing nothing, with the badge count and any explanation in the X-PosterOverlays-Badges and X-PosterOverlays-Note headers.

Housekeeping, with no change to how badges are drawn: the plugin now appears under "Movies & Shows" in the catalogue instead of "General", which is where something that draws on the posters of films, series, seasons and episodes belongs.

The category is not free text. The official catalogue uses exactly eight values, and one outside that set parses cleanly and then belongs to no filter at all - the plugin would quietly drop out of every category view with no error anywhere. The build now refuses a value outside those eight before it starts, rather than shipping one and finding out later.

Only the repository manifest is actually read for this, so it could have been changed without a release. It goes out as a version so the copy inside the package says the same thing: that copy is never displayed, but it does sit in the ZIP, so leaving the two apart would mean the package permanently disagrees with the catalogue it is listed in.

Added: two centred badge positions, "Top, centred" and "Bottom, centred", for images a client crops on the sides. Jellyfin's episode list shows a still in a container of its own proportions and takes the difference off the left and right, so a badge near either edge is cut in half - and raising the margin does not help, because the crop is proportional rather than a fixed number of pixels.

Centred sidesteps that instead of fighting it: the crop may take as much as it likes off both sides and a badge in the middle stays whole, so only the vertical distance still has to fit. The horizontal margin is ignored in these two positions, because a margin is a distance from an edge and there is none. With a vertical badge direction each pill is centred on its own rather than the column as a block.

Existing presets are unaffected: the new values are appended, so the four corners keep the meaning they had.

Added: "Kino Fassung" written as two words is now recognised as the theatrical cut. The catalogue only knew the compound spelling, so a folder that separated the words got no edition badge at all and instead turned up in the nightly report of edition-looking phrases with no rule for them. The optional space cannot widen the match - "kino" on its own still fires no rule.

Documented: the repair path never downloads from an image provider that is switched off for the library the item belongs to, and the code now says why that is not automatic. Passing the item does not restrict the providers by itself; "disabled" is defined relative to a library, so the item supplies the frame of reference and the query flag applies it. No behaviour change - the guard was already there, but it read like tidiness somebody could remove.

Changed: a folder that says two independent things now gets two edition badges. "REMASTERED.EXTENDED" used to draw EXT alone, because both rules matched and only the first was ever used.

Collecting every match would be wrong the other way round - it would turn "Extended Directors Cut" into three badges for one version. So each rule now declares what kind of statement it makes: which cut this is, how the picture is framed or coloured, how the copy was mastered. Within one kind the first match still wins, so a combination like EDC stays a single badge; across kinds the badges stand side by side, with the cut first because that is what tells two copies of a film apart.

Measured over 2380 real folders, six carry two edition tokens and no folder carries two of the same kind, so this is a small and predictable change.

Added: episodes are read from their file name, so two copies of one episode in the same resolution can finally be told apart. A movie keeps its release tags in its folder name, but a flattened season is one folder with every episode beside each other in it, so for episodes the file name is the only place they live. The episode title is subtracted first, exactly as a film title is - otherwise an ordinary title like "The Extended Family" would be read as an edition - and the remaining text must contain a known release tag or it is discarded whole. Movies are unaffected.

Added: records whose item no longer exists are cleared at the end of the nightly run, together with their cached originals. Until now they stayed on disk forever. This matters more than tidiness, because repairing a wrong metadata match recreates the entry under a new id. The sweep refuses to act when the library looks wrong rather than smaller, since a cached original is the only copy of an unbadged cover.

Fixed: the two completeness colour swatches showed black and picking a colour had no effect. The presets held empty strings written by an earlier load-time fault, and a colour input with no value renders as black - so an absence looked like a choice. A blank colour is now filled in with the default, and every reader of a colour treats blank and the default alike, so repairing the stored value redraws nothing.

Fixed: ticking "Color the badge by whether it holds throughout" looked like it showed the preview twice. It was showing both halves of that setting; both rows are captioned now.

Fixed: the step buttons beside the numeric fields are smaller and properly centred.

Fixes the settings page writing blanks over the selected preset while it was still loading - which is how a preset ended up named Unnamed with settings nobody chose. The number fields no longer rely on the browser spinner: it is replaced by two buttons so the spacing is actually set. Adds a floating preview pinned to the right edge that shows the selected style while it is being edited.

Fixes the settings page throwing the presets away on save. A plugin configuration travels through two serialisers: XmlSerializer writes the file and populates a read-only collection property, System.Text.Json carries it to and from the settings page and silently does not. The presets were on disk and on the page, and gone the moment Save was pressed, leaving every category pointing at a preset that no longer existed. A configuration already emptied by this repairs itself from the legacy settings, rebuilt under the same preset id, so the look key is unchanged and nothing already badged is redrawn. Also proper spacing between a number and its spinner arrows, a colour picker beside each completeness colour, and a preset saved without a name becomes Unnamed rather than an invisible entry.

Presets: how a badge looks is now a named preset that any category points at, with four read-only built-ins, duplicate-to-edit, and export/import of presets as JSON. Series, seasons and episodes are badged: what a series may claim is aggregated from its episodes, with several copies of one episode collapsed to the best first, so a show that is available throughout in 4K is not reported as mixed. Where it is genuinely mixed the badge is marked, by colour and by a marker that keeps the label readable. Episodes are badged only where two rows carry the same episode and nothing else tells them apart. Existing settings migrate unchanged: the movie look key is byte-identical, so nothing already badged is redrawn.

Rebuilds the repair task. It no longer searches for an inconsistent cache - that cannot find the damage, because a cache written by the faulty first release is consistent with its own record and merely describes an already badged image. It now works on scope: every item with a record plus every item that would be badged gets a fresh primary image from the metadata provider and is forgotten, so a following apply run badges it once, cleanly. A single-item route allows trying it on one poster first.

Internal correctness: everything the plugin and its build script persist now uses the invariant culture and ISO 8601 UTC explicitly. The build script formatted its timestamp without a culture, which is only correct on a machine whose culture uses a colon as the time separator - 21 do not. Nothing about the badges changes.

Changing the look of the badges now redraws the posters that already have them. Only the badge set was compared before, so a new style, corner, direction or size was reported as "already correct" and never applied to anything that was already done. Settings that do not change the image are kept out of that comparison, so saving an exclusion list does not order a redraw of the whole library.

Settings page layout: the exception boxes and the checkbox rows no longer depend on custom elements that a plugin page cannot rely on being registered, number fields are narrow and right aligned, and the three style previews replace the style dropdown instead of duplicating it.

Fixes the settings page, which did not initialise at all: its root element pointed at a controller module that does not exist instead of declaring the controls it needs, so nothing was upgraded and no value was ever loaded. Adds a 3D badge as its own category, so a film can be an extended cut and in 3D at the same time. Adds a direction setting, so the badges can run along the top or bottom edge in one row instead of stacking downwards. Adds a live preview of all three styles on the settings page.

versions.changelog:
## Developer
- Updated JPKribs.Jellyfin.Base to 2026.10.16.

## User
- The Refresh Guide progress is now more accurate

## User
- Channels now direct play on clients that support the stream instead of always being remuxed or transcoded by the server

## Developer
- The opened source now sets SupportsDirectPlay. PlaybackInfo always disables direct stream (MediaInfoHelper), so a source that only allowed direct stream could never be picked and every tune-in fell back to DirectPlayError and a remux

## User
- A channel with no viewers now stops when its countdown reaches zero. It used to run on for two to three minutes after the last viewer left
- Tune-in cards are generated for every channel shortly after the server starts and at every guide refresh, including the refresh a save triggers, so a fresh install, an update, a new logo, or changed output settings never leave a channel opening without its card

## Developer
- The linger teardown was vetoed every time because the Jellyfin reader is served right up to the close, so the two-minute recent-delivery rule always saw a viewer at the 30s mark, and the one-shot task then gave up until the reaper backstop 90s plus a minute later. A lingering session now only counts delivery after the close (DeliveryCountsAsWatched, unit tested), and LingerTeardownAsync retries every 5s until the reaper threshold
- LiveChannelsTvService sweeps the tune-in cards 20s after construction and from every GetChannelsAsync (EnsureLogoAsync then IntroService.EnsureAsync per enabled channel, serialised, logged with its trigger); a tune-in without a card now logs it
- The Sessions tab countdown wording no longer uses an em dash or a semicolon

## User
- Tune-in is now immediate. A channel opens on a short animated card (its logo and a Starting Channel caption over flowing lines) the moment you tune in, while the content is seeked and encoded behind it, and the picture no longer waits ten seconds or more for a buffer to fill first
- The Start-up buffer setting is gone. It turned out to be a literal pause Jellyfin applied before every tune-in rather than a buffer, and the cushion it was meant to provide is now built up while you are already watching

## Developer
- Removed StartupBufferSeconds and BufferMs (Jellyfin sleeps for BufferMs in TranscodeManager.AcquireResources before launching the delivery ffmpeg, on every tune-in including adoption)
- The tune-in handover now waits for the playlist and one segment instead of the full cushion, and the endpoint reader's hold-back ramps in one segment per ten seconds of session age instead of applying from the first byte
- Segments and the encoder GOP are now three seconds, matching Jellyfin's delivery remux so every stage cuts on the same keyframes

## Developer
- Bump base to 2026.07.31
- Rebuilt for Jellyfin 12.0 on .NET 10, with the target ABI raised to 12.0.0.0
- The dashboard menu entry now shows a live_tv icon instead of the generic folder
- CI builds, tests, and CodeQL now run on .NET 10, and label sync has the token scope it needs

versions.changelog:
Burger-menu på brede skærme.

Jellyfin 12 viser kun burger-knappen i smalle vinduer. Denne version lægger en
burger-knap i venstre side af app-baren på brede skærme også. Den åbner den
samme menu - med ekstra-punkterne øverst og Seerr Requests-linksene - og
skjules igen, mens en video spiller.

Slås til under "Burger menu on desktop screens". Ingen effekt på Jellyfin 10.11
eller i smalle vinduer.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Baggrundsbilledet på detaljesider lægger sig ikke længere oven på Jellyfins eget. Jellyfin tegner selv et baggrundsbillede i vinduer over 1000 px, og det kunne nå frem, mens vores stadig blev hentet - så lå der to lag og tonede hen over hinanden. Kontrollen sker nu lige før billedet sættes ind, i stedet for inden hentningen begynder.

Målt på Jellyfin 12: ved 1200 px vinder Jellyfins eget, ved 900 px vores. Begge dele sker, og i begge tilfælde vises nu præcis ét billede.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Baggrundsbilledet på detaljesider hentes nu i vinduets egen bredde i stedet for det dobbelte. På en skærm med skalering bad siden før om et 2560 px bredt billede til et 1268 px vindue; nu er det 1280 px - omkring en fjerdedel så mange bytes, og en størrelse serveren som regel har lavet i forvejen.

Billedet ligger bag et mørkt slør, hvor detaljerne alligevel ikke kan ses. Kort og plakater er uændrede: de ses tæt på og hentes stadig i skærmens egen opløsning.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Den natlige billedopvarmning tager nu kun titler, der er kommet til inden for de sidste 45 dage. Hele biblioteket køres igennem om søndagen, så billedstørrelser, en ny app begynder at bede om, stadig bliver lavet på forhånd.

Målt på serveren: den natlige kørsel så på 69.174 billeder for at lave 7.513 af dem og tog halvanden time, fordi resten allerede var lavet og kun blev tjekket.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Det første kort, du holder musen over efter en sideindlæsning, viser nu også forhåndsvisningen. Rækken kom på skærmen et halvt sekund før den begyndte at lytte efter musen, så den første bevægelse blev tabt - derfor virkede det næste kort med det samme, og det første bagefter.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Forhåndsvisningen på Fortsæt afspilning starter med det samme i stedet for efter tre sekunder, og klikker du på kortet, fortsætter afspilningen dér, hvor forhåndsvisningen er nået til.

I browsere uden forbindelse til serverens fjernbetjening starter klikket stadig - dér fra det gemte sted, et par sekunder før billedet på skærmen.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Et klik på Fortsæt afspilning afspiller med det samme, også i browsere hvor Jellyfins fjernbetjening ikke har forbindelse - dér endte klikket før på afsnittets side.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Forsiden står stille igen på Jellyfin 12.

- Fortsæt afspilning og Næste afsnit er én række igen, og Trending virker igen. Den gav op, når andre havde set mange afsnit den seneste måned.
- Rækkerne hopper ikke længere rundt, mens forsiden indlæses, og billederne på Fortsæt afspilning skifter ikke: de viser seriens billede, ligesom Jellyfins egen række.
- Ingen S/E-mærker på Fortsæt afspilning.
- Filmbibliotekernes redesign (Anbefalet til dig, favoritter og filtre) er fjernet, så bibliotekerne ser ud som i Jellyfin selv.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Hurtigere billeder overalt: forsiden, søgningen og detaljesiderne.

- Jellyfin laver et billede i en ny størrelse første gang, nogen beder om den, og det tager 0,1-0,5 sekunder pr. billede. Apps beder om lidt forskellige størrelser på hver enhed og i hvert vindue, så de fleste billeder blev lavet forfra. Størrelserne rundes nu til en kort liste, så et billede lavet til én enhed genbruges af den næste, og kvalitet over 90 sættes ned til 90 - et plakatkort fylder omkring en tredjedel mindre uden synlig forskel. Gælder alle apps.
- Ny planlagt opgave "Warm image cache" (dagligt kl. 03:00) laver plakater, baggrunde, logoer og skuespillerbilleder på forhånd i de størrelser, jeres apps faktisk bruger. Nye film og afsnit klares et par minutter efter, de er kommet ind. Opgaven sætter farten ned, når nogen bruger serveren. Første kørsel på et stort bibliotek tager et par timer.
- "Mere som dette" og samlinger på detaljesider huskes i 30 minutter pr. bruger. Jellyfin 12 bruger op til 1,5 sekund på at regne dem ud hver gang. De glemmes, så snart du ser eller markerer noget som favorit, eller biblioteket ændres.
- Søgningen henter skuespillere og instruktørens andre film, når du holder pause i skrivningen, i stedet for ved hvert tastetryk. Skuespillerne vises, så snart de er kendt, uden at vente på instruktørens film, billeder længere ude i rækkerne hentes først, når de kommer frem, og søger du på det samme igen, står det der med det samme.
- Mens plakater og portrætter hentes, vises en sløret udgave af billedet i stedet for en tom grå boks.
- Det hele kan slås fra under Speed i indstillingerne.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Afsnitsnummeret er tilbage på forsiden på Jellyfin 12.

- Når en serie har fået et nyt afsnit, viser Jellyfin 12 selve afsnittets kort i "Nyligt tilføjet" i stedet for seriens kort med antallet af usete afsnit. Det tal var det, New Badges skrev S/E-nummeret ind i, så mærket forsvandt. Afsnitskortene får nu selv et mærke med fx S4E7 samme sted og i samme stil.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.1.0.

Ingen dobbelt "Anmod om film eller serie" i sidemenuen på Jellyfin 12.

- Seerr Requests har sin egen Tilføj-knap i sidemenuen lige ovenover, så genvejen fra New Badges var den samme knap to gange. På Jellyfin 12 vises den ikke længere.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.0.0, hvor genvejen stadig findes.

Forsiden indlæses hurtigere.

- NEW-badges husker datoerne et kvarter, så forsiden ikke slår hver serie op igen, hver gang appen åbnes.
- Højst tre serieopslag ad gangen, så plakaterne ikke står i kø bag dem.
- Trending og den samlede Fortsæt-række vises med det samme fra sidste besøg og opdateres i baggrunden - også efter appen har været lukket.
- Samme række hentes ikke længere to gange på én gang.
- Om Seerr Requests er installeret, huskes et døgn.
- Scriptet caches af browseren og hentes kun igen, når plugin'et er opdateret.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.0.0.

Sidemenuen bliver nu lukket, når du bruger den på Jellyfin 12 - også efter genvejen til anmodninger, "Overrask mig" og Fortsæt med at se.

2.6.1.0 fik det ikke helt løst. Jellyfin 12 lukker selv sidemenuen, så snart du trykker på noget i den, og menuens baggrund virker som en kontakt: lukkes den en gang til, åbner den igen. Når New Badges eller Seerr Requests bagefter også lukkede menuen, sprang den derfor op igen. Nu lukker New Badges kun menuen, hvis den stadig er helt fremme, og genvejen til anmodninger holder Seerr Requests' ekstra lukning væk.

Genvejene i menuen har nu præcis samme skrift og placering som Jellyfins egne punkter.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.0.0, som virker uændret.

Sidemenuen lukker nu rigtigt når du bruger genvejen til anmodninger på Jellyfin 12, og genvejene i menuen har fået samme skrift som resten af menuen.

Genvejen til anmodninger åbnede den rigtige fane, men sidemenuen blev stående åben. Både New Badges og Seerr Requests lukkede menuen, lige efter hinanden - og en ekstra lukning mens menuen stadig er ved at glide ud, åbner den igen i stedet. Nu lukkes den kun én gang.

"Overrask mig" og genvejen til anmodninger stod med en anden, fed skrift end resten af menuen. De bruger nu samme skrift, størrelse og placering som Hjem og Favoritter.

Kun Jellyfin 12. På 10.11 bliver du på 2.3.0.0, som virker uændret.

Fire funktioner der holdt op med at virke på Jellyfin 12 virker igen, og NEW-mærket sidder ikke længere på skuespillere.

NEW på skuespillere og instruktører: Rækken "Cast & Crew" på en films side fik NEW på alle kort. En person i Jellyfin får en ny oprettelsesdato hver gang dens oplysninger opdateres, så alle skuespillere så nyligt tilføjede ud. Personer får aldrig NEW nu. Den fejl fandtes også på 10.11.

Genvejene i sidemenuen (hurtigsøgning, "Fortsæt afspilning", "Overrask mig" og genvejen til anmodninger): Jellyfin 12 har lavet sidemenuen om, og den gamle menu findes stadig i siden men bliver aldrig vist - så genvejene blev lagt et sted ingen kunne se dem. De sidder nu i den nye menu, lige under Hjem og Favoritter. Jellyfin 12 viser kun den menu på smalle skærme som telefoner.

Genvejen til anmodninger åbnede i nogle tilfælde Udgivelseskalenderen i stedet for anmodningssiden. Den rammer nu den rigtige fane.

Filmbibliotekets nye forside: Jellyfin 12 har ingen faneblade på filmsiden, og det var netop fanebladet forsiden blev sat ind i. Den dukker nu op igen i stedet for Jellyfins eget gitter.
